In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
choledochal malformations are associated with a high incidence of malignancy.
all choledochal patients, whether symptomatic or asymptomatic, should be treated by surgical excision of the cyst, and that a careful search be made for neoplasm at operation.
choledochal malformation is a risk factor for the development of neoplasms in the biliary tree and the pancreas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
choledochal malformations are associated with a high incidence of biliary tract neoplasms.
the incidence of choledochocarcinomas and cholangiocarcinomas is high in choledochal patients, and that these neoplasms are more likely to develop at an earlier age than the general population.
the choledochoduodenal junction is the most common site for malignancy to form, and the incidence of malignancy is high in patients who have an anomalous pancreaticobiliary junction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a choledochal dilatation in an adult patient should raise the suspicion of an anomalous pancreaticobiliary junction.
all patients with choledochal disease should be followed up indefinitely.
choledochal malformations should be treated surgically as early as possible, and that a high index of suspicion for neoplasia is required.
